skill.name: pytest-mock-guide
skill.description: Practical guide for using pytest-mock to patch, spy, stub, and assert mocked behavior in pytest tests.
skill.summary: Use pytest-mock patterns to write focused Python tests with reliable mocks.
skill.author: bossjones

static_findings.snippet: pytest-mock is a pytest plugin providing a `mocker` fixture as a thin wrapper around Python's `unitt
The `mocker` fixture is the main interface. Request it in your test function:
| `class_mocker` | class | Share mocks across test class |
| `module_mocker` | module | Share mocks across test module |
| `session_mocker` | session | Share mocks across entire session |
Same as `patch.object` but doesn't warn when mock is used as context manager:
| `return_value` | Value returned when mock is called |
| `side_effect` | Exception to raise or function to call |
| `spec_set` | Stricter spec that prevents setting new attributes |
| `spy_return` | Last return value from real method |

content.value_statement: Mocking in pytest can be hard to apply correctly across patches, spies, stubs, and async tests. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused pytest-mock guidance for reliable test doubles.
actual_capabilities: Explains the mocker fixture and available fixture scopes.
Shows how to patch functions, objects, dictionaries, and multiple attributes.
Guides use of spies, stubs, autospec, and assertion helpers.
Covers async mocks, context managers, properties, and fixture composition.
Describes mock lifecycle controls such as stop, stopall, and resetall.
limitations: Does not execute tests or inspect your project automatically.
Assumes pytest and pytest-mock are already available in the environment.
Examples are instructional and may need adaptation for your module paths.
Does not replace pytest documentation for version-specific behavior.

use_cases.title: Patch Dependencies in Unit Tests
use_cases.description: Mock imports, functions, and object attributes while keeping tests focused on one behavior.

use_cases.title: Verify Calls and Side Effects
use_cases.description: Use spies, stubs, and call assertions to validate interactions without hitting real services.

use_cases.title: Design Async Mocking Patterns
use_cases.description: Plan async mocks, awaited assertions, and async context manager tests for service code.

prompt_templates.title: Start with Patching
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to patch a function with pytest-mock in a simple test.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Patch Method
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose between mocker.patch, patch.object, patch.dict, and patch.multiple for this dependency.

prompt_templates.title: Review Mock Assertions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my test plan for spies, autospec, async mocks, and fixture-scoped patches.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Complex Test Doubles
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a pytest-mock strategy for a service with database, cache, and external API dependencies.

output_examples.input: I need to patch a module function in pytest.
output_examples.output: Use mocker.patch at the import location where the function is used. Assert the replacement received the expected arguments.

output_examples.input: My test needs to observe a real method call.
output_examples.output: Use a spy when real behavior should run while call history and return values are inspected.

output_examples.input: I have async callbacks and context managers.
output_examples.output: Use async stubs or AsyncMock patterns, then assert awaited calls instead of normal call assertions.

best_practices: Patch objects where the system under test imports them.
Use autospec or spec_set when mocks should match real interfaces.
Keep mock scope as small as the behavior under test allows.
anti_patterns: Patching the definition module when the code uses an imported alias.
Using broad session mocks when a function-scoped mock would isolate state.
Asserting only that a mock was called without checking meaningful arguments.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps apply pytest-mock patterns for patching, spying, stubbing, and assertions in Python tests.

faq.question: Does it require pytest-mock?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance assumes the pytest-mock plugin and its mocker fixture are available.

faq.question: Can it help with async tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes async stubs, AsyncMock usage, awaited assertions, and async context manager patterns.

faq.question: Does it run my tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples but does not execute commands or inspect project files.

faq.question: Can it replace official pytest docs?
faq.answer: No. It is a practical guide and should be checked against version-specific documentation when needed.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
